chats.answer:
If you're looking for the best split-phase inverter generator, I'd prioritize models that provide 120V/240V output, clean inverter power, and enough capacity for home backup.

The important distinction is that not every inverter generator supports 240V. Many popular portable inverter generators only produce 120V, making them unsuitable for powering 240V well pumps, HVAC equipment, or other large appliances.

For a whole-home or partial-home backup setup, I'd focus on generators with at least 7,000–10,000 running watts, depending on your electrical loads.

What I'd choose

For the best balance of price and output, Westinghouse ecoGen10000 is my first choice. For fuel flexibility and higher power, I'd choose the Champion 201417. If quiet operation matters most and budget is secondary, I'd choose the Honda EU7000iS.

One important detail: a 50A receptacle doesn't mean the generator can continuously supply 50A at 240V. Actual output is limited by running wattage. A licensed electrician should install a suitable transfer switch or interlock, and the generator must run outdoors away from openings.

One question: Are you buying this for home backup through a 120/240V electrical panel, or for a 240V appliance such as a well pump, air conditioner, or EV charger? That changes which generator I'd recommend.

For most buyers, I recommend looking at generators in the 7,000–11,000 running-watt range, depending on your power requirements.

What matters for split-phase operation

Check that the generator has a 120/240V L14-30R or 14-50R outlet, sufficient running wattage on your chosen fuel, and a neutral/ground configuration compatible with your transfer equipment. A 50A outlet does not necessarily mean the generator can continuously deliver 50A.

For home backup, use a properly installed transfer switch or interlock; never backfeed a receptacle. Run the generator outdoors, well away from doors, windows, and vents.
